newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS BUT WIBERG STEALS SHOW.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS BUT WIBERG STEALS SHOW.

text.p: Italian Olympic champion Deborah Compagnoni clinched her first giant slalom victory of the Alpine skiing season on Friday but the talk of the German slopes was World Cup leader Pernilla Wiberg.

Compagnoni, the reigning world champion, produced an aggressive but composed performance on a bumpy German piste to win her second World Cup race of the season, 1.16 seconds faster than second-placed Austrian Anita Wachter over the two runs.
But Wiberg, who is proving herself to be a real all-rounder this season, managed third place -- her best finish in a giant slalom since 1993.

The performance helped the Swede to stretch her lead over Germany's defending champion Katja Seizinger in the overall World Cup standings by 60 points to 274. Seizinger had a calamitous day after a fall in the second run.

After some disappointing results in giant slalom in recent seasons, Wiberg wanted to show she could still produce the goods in the discipline in which she won gold at the 1992 Albertville Olympics. She proved it emphatically on her main rival's home ground.
Seizinger, who was the joint leader of the giant slalom standings at the start of the day, crashed out of the second run after a mistake at the top of the course.

Second-fastest in the first run, the German ended up looking like a novice as she hurtled down the course with her head in the snow and her boots out of her skis after hitting a gate. The German was unhurt but frustrated.
"It certainly wasn't a soft landing," she said. "But anything can happen when you take risks."

The course was icy in parts but Compagnoni, who had twice finished second in the discipline in races in Maribor, Slovenia, and the Austrian resort of Soelden, looked in complete control as she clocked an aggregate two minutes 8.45 seconds.
The Italian was 1.08 seconds ahead of Seizinger after the first run with Wachter in third, 1.34 seconds behind.
Wachter, who won the last race in this German resort in 1991, clocked an overall 2:09.61 with Wiberg third in 2:09.92, 1.47 seconds behind the leader.
Compagnoni also won a slalom in Semmering, Austria, on December 29 -- her first ever victory on the circuit in the technical discipline.
Like Seizinger, Italy's Sabina Panzanini had a bad day after starting the day equal with the German at the top of the giant slalom standings.
Panzanini, who had won two of the three previous giant slaloms, looked uncomfortable on the course and was unable to make an impact after finishing 19th in the first run.
